# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-01-23

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-01-23-rp-some-fun-games-in-the-divisional-round.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

Third [[Matt Harmon]] episode ingested, with co-host **James Koh** (not
tracked). A Divisional Round recap across all four games — Chiefs-Bills,
49ers-Packers, Bucs-Lions, Ravens-Texans — heavier on team-building/free-agency
speculation than the two prior episodes. Per the low-durability guidance for
game-recap content, coaching-carousel speculation (Sean McDermott's job
security, a hypothetical Ben Johnson-to-Buffalo pitch, Bill Belichick landing
spots) was **not** ingested; forward-looking player evaluations and free-agency
mechanisms were.

**Buffalo:** heavy [[Stefon Diggs]] material — a specific unreported-injury
theory (oblique/back/abdominal, first flagged in Week 10, aggravated in the
Wild Card win), a steep first-half-season-to-second-half production collapse
(11.3 targets/93.5 yards/game through 8 games to 7.9 targets/43 yards/game and
one total touchdown over the final 8), and $32M in dead cap ruled out as a cut
candidate — restructure or trade seen as the likely paths. [[Gabe Davis]] gets
a free-agency read as a clear "not a true number two receiver," rotational
piece. [[Khalil Shakir]] gets reinforcing praise as a building block.

**Green Bay:** the fullest breakdown yet of the WR room hierarchy — [[Jayden Reed]] and [[Dontayvion Wicks]] rated the two receivers with real paths to a
true WR1 role, [[Christian Watson]]'s case explicitly reduced to "size and
speed" alone, [[Romeo Doubs]] pegged a clear fourth. [[Aaron Jones]] gets
extended praise ("criminally underrated") alongside a durability concern and a
call for Green Bay to address the RB2 spot. [[Jordan Love]] gets reinforcing
top-10-quarterback praise.

**San Francisco:** an extended, opinionated [[Brock Purdy]] discourse
breakdown — Harmon's explicit verdict is a bad game (poor grip/accuracy in
wet conditions, a specific playmaker-gene comparison to [[Tua Tagovailoa]]),
paired with a "good, but not elite-tier — top 20" season-long grade. A light
new [[Jared Goff]] note on quarterback mental development is used as the
optimistic comp for Purdy's own growth curve.

**Tampa Bay:** free-agency mechanics for [[Mike Evans]] (expected 3-year,
$50M+ market, Detroit's cap space and Dan Campbell's culture floated as a
fit) and [[Baker Mayfield]] (contract-tier discussion, expectation he stays
in Tampa rather than face a 7th head coach).

**Houston:** [[Nico Collins]] reinforced as a top-10 receiver with a specific
mechanism (Baltimore boxing him up outside of scheme, 47 of his 68 yards
coming after the catch). [[Devin Singletary]] has a bad divisional-round
game (9 carries, 22 yards, -25 rush yards over expected) that Harmon frames
against a strong prior stretch, with Houston still flagged as needing to add
a back. [[John Metchie III]] gets a harsher read than his Wild Card flash —
"proven nothing to this point in his career." [[Noah Brown]]'s IR absence is
confirmed as a real loss, not just a name removed from availability. [[C.J. Stroud]] gets his first real caveat in this wiki — looked like a rookie
against Baltimore's disguised coverages with no counterpunch once Nico
Collins was taken away.

**Not given pages/updates:** Bo Melton (one-line, non-substantive "can't stop
scoring touchdowns" praise), Trent Sherfield, Deontay Harty, Robert Woods
(depth-piece mentions only), DeAndre Hopkins (used only as a comparison point
for Mike Evans's culture fit, not his own evaluation), Chris Godwin and
Brandon Aiyuk and Deebo Samuel (mentioned, but nothing beyond what's already
on their pages). A long McDermott/Ben-Johnson/Belichick coaching-carousel
discussion was not ingested.
